_comment: League setup, per game. Read by the toolkit (Auction panel) and, later, by the shipped engine.
Its one job is the REPLACEMENT LEVEL: the fantamedia of the marginal rostered player at a role.
VALUE = FM x Pv is the sum of a season's fantavoti, which is the right currency only if the
alternative to fielding a player were fielding nobody. You field 11 of 25, so whoever does not
play is replaced by a bench player worth roughly the role's own level - and what a player is
actually worth is (FM - replacement) x Pv. That needs no fitted coefficient, only how many
players of each role a league rosters, which is league configuration, not a model parameter.
NOT YET GATED: the pre-registered gate protects FM MAE and VALUE MAE, and neither moves when the
sort key changes. The Auction panel therefore offers it as a second ranking, defaulting to VALUE.
_reliability_note: SURPLUS x (Pv / matchdays)^exponent. You set the lineup BEFORE knowing whether he plays, so what
you actually collect is not his appearances - it is the appearances you could see coming. That is a
measurable quantity, not a taste, and it was measured: on the dated per-matchday layer, availability
carries real memory (persistence 0.29-0.36 on all four platform-seasons, never near 0), and the share
of a player's own appearances that a naive 'field him if he played last week' rule catches runs from
0.39-0.41 for the under-20% band to 0.88-0.90 for the over-80% band.
(Pv/matchdays)^0.5 reproduces that curve within a few points across every band, which is why the
exponent is 0.5 - it is the fitted shape of catchability, NOT a risk-aversion knob. Raise it if you
also want risk aversion on top; 0 turns the whole thing off and gives back the exact expected surplus.
Applies to the SURPLUS currency only; VALUE = FM x Pv, the pre-registered gate metric, is untouched.
_min_availability_note: Minimum share of the season a player must have to be RANKED in an auction top ten at all.
The weight above is a discount and a discount can always be out-earned: one match at 9.5 keeps 18%
of a small surplus, which in a role where scarcity is near zero is still enough to place 7th. That is
not a valuation error, it is a category error - a man who played once is not a player you could have
fielded, so he does not belong in a ranking of who to buy, at any discount. Hence a floor and not a
steeper curve. 0.35 is about 13 matchdays of 38 and 11 of 31, just under the Pv >= 15 domain the FM
core itself was fitted on, so nothing below it was ever a validated estimate anyway.
It gates the RANKING only: the player keeps his row, his numbers and his real rank everywhere else,
and VALUE lists are not filtered at all - they are the pre-registered deliverable.
_mantra_note: Mantra depth is DERIVED, never tabulated here. The rule above fixes each group's total ('eight
defenders'); the SHAPE inside the group comes from the fielding caps a Mantra module imposes - no
scheme lets you field 3 'pc' or 4 'dc' - and those caps are MEASURED off real starting elevens by
`features.simultaneous_caps` rather than transcribed from the official module table. Read at the
90th percentile, because a multi-role starter counts in every role he is listed with; the measurement
returns dc 3 and pc 2, which is exactly what the modules allow. A third measured factor converts the
rule's PLAYERS into the pool's LISTINGS (a 'dc;dd' defender is one of the eight but two listings).
Result on euro/mantra 24-25, 8 teams: por 24 deep (= 8 x 3, the Classic rule reproduced exactly, as
it must be for the one role that overlaps with nothing), dc 32, dd/ds 21, b 11, e/m/c 29, w/t/pc 13,
a 20. SURPLUS then keeps 23 of 70 names against VALUE's 22, where the even split kept 21.
Two things NOT to mistake for defects. A replacement level above the role ANCHOR is expected: the
anchor is the perimeter's mean, this is the marginal ROSTERED player, and a league picking from 39
usable 'pc' rosters above-average strikers. And two roles still exhaust their pool - 'b' (11 deep, 8
usable braccetti) and Serie A's 'por' (24 deep, 18 keepers with Pv >= 20) - so their level is 'the
worst regular', which is the honest answer when the league cannot actually roster that deep.
Rejected on measurement, recorded so it is not retried: splitting a group in proportion to the
SIBLING POOL sizes. It fixes dc but drives the small pools 'pc' and 't' to rank 8, +0.72 and +0.76
above their anchors - worse than the even split it replaced. Pool size cannot know that a defensive
slot is far likelier to be a centre-back than a braccetto; only the cap knows that.
`mantra_slots` below overrides the derivation per role, for a league that really rosters differently.
An even split of each group is the offline fallback, used only when there are no lineups to measure.
